statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n - k + 1 and, for every s with 0 <= s <= n-k, r[s] = beauty(s), where for a start s we let W_s be the multiset {nums[i] | s <= i < s+k}, let N_s be the sub-multiset of negative elements of W_s, and let beauty(s) be 0 if |N_s| < x, and otherwise the x-th element of N_s sorted nondecreasingly (1-indexed, with equal values counted with multiplicity).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums is nonempty: 1 <= n <= 100000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -50 <= nums[i] <= 50. The i64 arguments k and x, regarded as mathematical integers, satisfy 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k.

statement: For any x1 and x2 with 1 <= x1 < x2 <= k, whenever get_subarray_beauty(nums,k,x1) returns r1 and get_subarray_beauty(nums,k,x2) returns r2, for every s with 0 <= s <= n-k, if the window nums[s..s+k) contains at least x2 negative entries, then r1[s] <= r2[s].

statement: For any two such slices nums and nums', if for every s with 0 <= s <= n-k the multiset of negative values in nums[s..s+k) equals the multiset of negative values in nums'[s..s+k) including multiplicities, then whenever get_subarray_beauty(nums,k,x) returns r and get_subarray_beauty(nums',k,x) returns r', it holds that for every s with 0 <= s <= n-k, r[s] = r'[s].
